open_points.subject: token-to-project relationship
open_points.text: every operation on a project needs the token.
open_points.question: Is the token a project-specific entity/capability, a global credential merely supplied alongside a project, or another value, and who mints it from what source facts?
options: One token is minted for and identifies or authorizes exactly one project.
A globally minted token authorizes operations across projects.
The token is an opaque caller-supplied value whose relationship to a project is checked elsewhere.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the token as a project-specific capability minted from the project's identity.

witness.initial: Projects A and B exist, and the caller has a token obtained while working with project A.
events: The caller asks the deliverer to scan project B's folder using that token.
outcomes: The scan is rejected because the token is bound to project A.
The scan proceeds because the token is global or is not intrinsically bound to a project.
witness.observer: The caller and the owner of project B

open_points.subject: token requirement for deliver and publication actions
open_points.text: every operation on a project needs the token.
open_points.question: Which of the three offered operations count as being "on a project," particularly deliver-one-photo and record-publication when their stated inputs do not explicitly name a project?
options: All three operations are project operations and always require the token.
Only scan explicitly operates on a project; deliver and record require a token only when separately given project context.
Project scope is inferred from the photo, placement, or publication, so deliver and record require the token only after that association exists.
open_points.default_guess: Treat all three offered operations as project-scoped and require the token for each.

witness.initial: A photo has been found in a confirmed project folder and is ready for delivery.
events: The caller invokes deliver-one-photo without passing explicit project context or a token.
outcomes: Delivery is rejected because every offered operation is implicitly on a project.
Delivery proceeds because the operation as invoked is not explicitly on a project.
witness.observer: The caller and the project owner
